At the edge of the world, to the direction of NorthEast, where the continent of Rilrel freezes beneath the shadow of the Great Ice Wall, lies the Old Dwarven Capital of Thiriel. It is an empire of eternal winter, for it stands farthest from the [[Birth Fire Island\|Birth Fire Island]] at the world’s heart. Snow never melts here, for Thiriel stands in eternal winter and the mountains stand tall in cold silence. Yet in this desolate place, life was once born of flame and stone. 

![](data:image/png;base64,)

In the beginning, the Titan Aberdeen shaped the first dwarves. From stone he carved dwarven statues, and into their faces he set jewels for eyes. When all was done, Aberdeen breathed his fiery essence into their forms, and stone turned to flesh. Thus came the dwarves, unyielding as the mountains, enduring as the cold. 

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Long before dwarves walked the land, Cerise - The Ardent Dragon Queen, ruled this frozen continent. She was said to coil her body around its peaks, her breath carving rivers of fire into the earth and splitting sky itself. Yet when Aberdeen’s children made their appearance, she did not fought them. Instead, she blessed their existence, watching as they built their homes, and halls of stone and metal. Then, with the coming of the unknown Great Sickness that nearly wiped the dwarven race, Cerise vanished. 

The disease struck like a lightining, sudden and fast, and few of Aberdeen’s creations endured it. Today, only Three High Kings remain, and their kin are but shadows of a people once vast and mighty. The few dwarves alive are known as the Firstborn, children born after the sickness who carry in their blood a strange immunity. To Thalori, who now fill the cities and encompass masses of Thiriel, the dwarves are a legendary race. Though the Thalori claim Thiriel as home, for their ancestors were born upon this frozen soil, they look upon the dwarves as the rightful kings, heirs of divine flame. Rumors has it, that it was the arrival of the Thalori themselves that carried the disease across the sea. 

At the heart of the kingdom burns the spirit of Thiriel itself: the Elder Forge, an ancient spirit of metal and flame. Here, beneath vaulted halls, the High Kings shape weapons not by hammer alone but through cooperation with elder spirit. Each weapon forged carries the name of its destined wielder, written in fire upon the blade. The steel then awakens, glowing with one of three lights: 

- White for future Justiciars that bring light to people and suffering to evil. 

- Red for fiery courage, these people wield the power of destruction, might intended to protect weak and punish darkness. 

- Purple for selfless saviors that shield women and children from a giant beasts of Thiriel. 

In Thiriel dwarves remain both rulers and living relics, now firstborn of stone, kings of a land that mourns its own fading legend.
